To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

chronic Cd exposure in monkeys with normal Ca status increased the blastogenic responses to Con A and PHA and that Cd exposure decreased the response to Con A and increased the response to PHA in monkeys with Ca-deficiency.
chronic dietary cadmium exposure in normal monkeys increases the cell-mediated immunity, whereas, chronic dietary cadmium in calcium deficient monkeys decreases the cell-mediated immunity.
chronic dietary Cd exposure in Ca deficient Rhesus monkeys resulted in a significant decrease in cell-mediated immune response.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of Ca deficiency in the immunotoxic effects of chronic Cd in male rhesus monkeys.
the role of Ca deficiency in modulating the immunotoxicity of Cd exposure.
the effect of dietary chronic Cd exposure on cell mediated immune response in R. monkeys and role of Ca deficiency.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Ca deficiency in monkeys exposed to Cd for a period of ten weeks resulted in significant immunosuppression.
Cd is an environmental pollutant that has the ability to modulate the immune response of the host.
the immunotoxicity of Cd may be modulated by nutritional deficiencies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Cd exposure in normal Ca status monkeys increased the blastogenic capacity in response to Con A.
Cd-induced immunosuppression in monkeys is due to the interaction of Cd and Ca in the host.
the immunosuppressive effects of Cd in the monkeys are due to the Ca deficiency induced by Cd exposure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Ca deficiency in monkeys exposed to Cd produced a further decrease in the blastogenesis of PBL to Con A.
Ca deficiency in monkeys exposed to Cd may have an adverse effect on the immune system, which can be further aggravated by Cd exposure.
Cd exposure in Ca deficient monkeys significantly decreased the blastogenesis of PBL in response to T cell mitogens, PHA and Con A.
